A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DualReg research. Their text, equations, figures and tables are readable, including v2's supplementary material. Material relocated from v1's main text can be matched reliably to v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original registration experiments on 3DMatch, 3DLoMatch and KITTI, including quantitative comparisons and component ablations in Tables I–V.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark experiments and ablations, and adds runtime, normal-estimation and parameter-sensitivity results in its supplement.

M1.justification: Equations (1) and (5) tighten the length-consistency condition from DL < 2τ to DL < τ, while both versions specify τ as three times the point-cloud resolution. This is a limited reported filtering change. The one-point filtering, weighted three-point refinement, geometric proxies and dual-space optimization otherwise remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate rigid registration on 3DMatch, 3DLoMatch and KITTI using FPFH and FCGF features. V2's additional analyses stratify existing data or vary processing and parameters; they do not establish additional dataset, domain or task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds PointDSC and VBReg across all three datasets and both feature types, substantially broadening the comparison to learning-based registration methods. Supplementary Table 5 also adds angular-difference filtering as a comparator. TurboReg was already evaluated in v1 and is retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds systematic parameter sweeps, normal-estimation controls using K = 10, 20 and 30 and Open3D versus PyMeshLab, and evaluation stratified by inlier ratio. It specifies GPU execution for PointDSC, VBReg and TurboReg and separates their timings from CPU rankings. The reported filtering cutoff also changes, while benchmark success criteria remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing component ablations are retained, with v1 Tables IV–V corresponding to v2 Tables 3 and 2. Supplement B adds stage-wise runtime analysis, recall/error and iteration-count curves across inlier ratios, angular-filter and normal-estimator comparisons, and sensitivity analyses for five parameters (Tables 4–6 and Figures 8–9).

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's additional curves and average runtimes do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial baseline, runtime and robustness results. Existing values also change: DualReg's 3DLoMatch/FCGF recall changes from 60.47% to 60.86% and RMSE from 7.76 to 7.81 cm; TurboReg's 3DMatch/FPFH RMSE changes from 5.03 to 4.99 cm (v1 Tables I–II; v2 Table 1). Given the filtering-cutoff revision, the DualReg changes are revised reported results rather than established same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The formal consensus-set definitions in Equations (1) and (5) change through the stricter length threshold. Beyond this limited mathematical revision, the reflection/SVD derivation and optimization formulation are retained, partly relocated to Supplement A; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the same central contributions: progressive correspondence filtering, anchor-based geometric proxies and joint feature/geometric optimization. The headline claim of approximately 32-fold CPU speedup over MAC on KITTI with comparable accuracy is also retained. Rewriting does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Supplement B adds substantive interpretations of parameter stability, normal-estimation robustness, computational tradeoffs and overlap-dependent parameter choices. The conclusion explains very-low-inlier failures through the assumption that the inlier set exceeds competing outlier clusters. V1's discussion of nonadaptive proxy radii and unused color information is removed.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page pointer, demo-video references, RTX 3090 hardware information and the default normal-estimation neighborhood K = 20. Most existing implementation and hyperparameter details move to Supplement A. Conversely, v1's explicit eight-scene 3DMatch and 555-pair KITTI test descriptions are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 adds six references covering robust loss, iteratively reweighted least squares, Anderson acceleration, non-rigid registration and Open3D, with a limited expansion of the robust-estimation discussion. The central positioning against TCF and maximal-clique methods remains. Publication updates for existing citations are not new works.

P1.justification: Substantial editing and compression accompany a reorganization into main text and supplementary sections. Detailed symmetry mathematics, pseudocode, refinement procedures, settings and extended benchmark discussion move to the supplement. Related-work and conclusion passages are rewritten, and section organization and terminology are revised.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different document layout, merges the three benchmark tables into Table 1, reformats the ablation tables and relocates expanded qualitative comparison grids to the supplement. V1's tangential-distance schematic is removed. New runtime and robustness displays appear in Tables 4–6 and Figures 8–9.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens empirical support by addressing validation gaps in v1: it evaluates learning-based comparators and directly examines normal-estimation choices and parameter dependence (Table 1, Tables 5–6 and Figure 9). Runtime breakdowns and hardware annotations also make efficiency claims easier to assess. These gains outweigh the loss of some limitations detail, although the unexplained cutoff revision prevents treating changed scores as clean performance improvements.
